# Requirements, by kind
163 atomic requirements from `../kit/requirements.json`, each with the diagram that realises it and the scenarios that verify it (from `pumllint trace`). Ids are stable; a statement is the contract, the rationale says why it reads that way. `basis` records how the requirement was derived when the kit was written: `logic` from the code's control flow, `prose` from a comment or docstring, `both`.

## Contracts: shapes, files, grammars (48)

### JDL-001 · contract · basis both
The universe loader shall read a TOML document whose only permitted top-level keys are `defaults` (a table) and `asset` (an array of tables); when no path is given it shall read the packaged `universe.toml` (shipped verbatim in contracts/universe.toml) and label it `packaged universe.toml` in messages, otherwise it shall label it with the path exactly as given.

*Realised by:* component, sync_run  
*Verified by:* sync.feature: The packaged universe expands into nine ordered legs; universe.feature: The packaged universe lists its six pilot assets

### JDL-002 · contract · basis logic
The `[defaults]` table shall accept only the keys `store` (default `data`) and `currency` (default `USD`); each, when present, shall be a non-empty string, and an absent `[defaults]` table shall resolve to those two defaults.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-003 · contract · basis logic
Each `[[asset]]` table shall accept only the keys `name`, `asset_class`, `currency`, `threshold`, `enabled` and `source`; `name` and `asset_class` are required non-empty strings, `currency` defaults to the `[defaults]` currency, `enabled` defaults to true, and `source` is a non-empty array of tables.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-004 · contract · basis both
The universe shall accept exactly three `asset_class` values and map each to the store `asset_type`: `stock` -> `stock`, `crypto` -> `crypto`, `bond_etf` -> `etf`; the store asset_type vocabulary is the sorted set of mapped values `['crypto', 'etf', 'stock']`.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape; universe.feature: The packaged universe lists its six pilot assets

### JDL-005 · contract · basis both
When an asset carries `threshold`, the loader shall accept any integer or float (not a boolean) and carry it as a float; when absent it shall default to -0.05; the value is documentation only and shall drive no behaviour of any command.

*Why:* the per-class threshold stays a conscious later knob; it is carried as documentation and never read by the loader

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-006 · contract · basis logic
Each `[[asset.source]]` table shall accept only the keys `provider`, `symbol`, `path`, `exchange`, `start`, `end`, `kind`, `enabled`, `modeled` and `note`; `provider` (one of `eodhd`, `binance`, `yahoo-csv`) and `symbol` are required non-empty strings, `kind` defaults to `eod`, `enabled` to true, `modeled` to false, `note` is an optional non-empty string, and the source inherits the asset's currency.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-007 · contract · basis both
When a source declares no `exchange`, the loader shall set the store partition tag from the provider: `eodhd` -> `eodhd`, `binance` -> `binance`, `yahoo-csv` -> `yahoo`; a declared `exchange` shall be a non-empty string and is used verbatim as the store partition tag.

*Why:* the venue tag, not a listing exchange - the EODHD listing exchange lives in the symbol suffix

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* sync.feature: The packaged universe expands into nine ordered legs; universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-008 · contract · basis logic
When a collector source (eodhd, binance) declares `start` or `end`, the loader shall normalise a TOML local date, or a string accepted by Python 3.11+ `date.fromisoformat` (e.g. `2024-01-02` or `20240102`), to `YYYY-MM-DD`; a TOML date-time shall be carried as its full ISO text (e.g. `2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00`); an absent key shall be carried as null.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-009 · contract · basis logic
When a source's provider is `yahoo-csv`, the loader shall require `path` (non-empty string, resolved relative to the working directory at run time) and shall carry no `start`/`end` keys; when the provider is `eodhd` or `binance` the loader shall carry `start` and `end` (possibly null) and no `path`.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-010 · contract · basis both
The loader shall enforce the modeled-source marker per asset: a `modeled = true` source must be enabled; at most one enabled source may be modeled; an enabled asset with two or more enabled sources must mark exactly one modeled; an enabled asset must have at least one enabled source; a disabled asset is exempt from the two last rules.

*Why:* the series that feeds the binning must be deterministic per enabled asset

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: The listing marks paused assets, switched-off sources and notes

### JDL-011 · contract · basis logic
The loader shall return one normalised document `{"defaults": {"store", "currency"}, "assets": [...]}` where each asset carries `name`, `asset_class`, `asset_type`, `currency`, `threshold` (float), `enabled` and `sources`, and each source carries `provider`, `kind`, `enabled`, `modeled`, `exchange`, `symbol`, `currency`, then `note` only when declared, then either `path` (yahoo-csv) or `start` and `end` (collector sources), in universe file order.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: Defaults, dates and the class map normalise into one shape

### JDL-023 · contract · basis both
Every collector shall perform HTTP through a transport offering `request(method, url, params)` returning a response carrying `status` and `text` (TransportResponse) and `close()`; the live transport shall use a requests session with a 30 s timeout and convert connection errors and timeouts into a retryable TransportConnectionError whose text has the token redacted; each collector shall rate-limit live traffic to 1000 requests per sliding 60 s window (sleeping until the oldest request leaves the window) and 100000 per UTC day, beyond which it raises DailyBudgetExhausted `daily API budget of 100000 spent ({UTC date}); the per-minute window cannot lend quota across days`.

*Why:* the daily quota is enforced as a daily budget, not fed in as a per-minute rate

*Realised by:* component, data_model  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: The replayer keys on file content, walks subdirectories and skips manifest.json

### JDL-024 · contract · basis both
The recorded-fixture identity of a request shall be `{"method": METHOD upper-cased, "path": the URL's path component, "params": {name: str(value)}}` over the request parameters minus `api_token`, sorted by name.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A request no fixture answers fails the leg and names what is known; collectors.feature: EODHD bars drop glitch rows, keep the first duplicate and sort by date; collectors.feature: Every recorded fixture of the kit is named and laid out by its request identity

### JDL-025 · contract · basis logic
The fixture recorder shall write one file per request named `{slug}_{digest}.json` where slug is the key's path with leading/trailing `/` stripped and inner `/` replaced by `_`, and digest is the first 10 hex characters of SHA-256 over `json.dumps(key, sort_keys=True)` (Python default separators, ASCII-escaped) encoded UTF-8; the file content shall be `json.dumps({"request": key, "response": {"status": int, "json": body}}, indent=1, sort_keys=True)` plus a newline, and recording shall refuse with CollectorError `refusing to write fixture: secret material in {path} response/request` when a registered secret occurs in that text.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Every recorded fixture of the kit is named and laid out by its request identity

### JDL-026 · contract · basis both
The fixture replayer shall load every `*.json` file under its directory recursively except files named `manifest.json`, key each by its `request` object, answer a matching request with the recorded `status` and the recorded `json` re-serialised as text, and raise CollectorError `no recorded fixture for {METHOD} {path} {params dict}` followed by a newline, `known fixtures:` and one line per known key (`  {path} {params dict}`, sorted) for any other request.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A request no fixture answers fails the leg and names what is known; collectors.feature: EODHD bars drop glitch rows, keep the first duplicate and sort by date; collectors.feature: The replayer keys on file content, walks subdirectories and skips manifest.json

### JDL-029 · contract · basis both
The EODHD collector shall call `GET {base}/eod/{SYM}` with params `api_token`, `fmt=json`, `period=d`, `order=a`, plus `from={start}` and `to={end}` only when given; `GET {base}/splits/{SYM}` and `GET {base}/div/{SYM}` with `api_token` and `fmt=json` only; base defaults to `https://eodhd.com/api` with any trailing `/` removed, so recorded fixture paths are `/api/eod/{SYM}`, `/api/splits/{SYM}`, `/api/div/{SYM}`.

*Realised by:* component, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: EODHD bars drop glitch rows, keep the first duplicate and sort by date

### JDL-032 · contract · basis both
When the EODHD `/eod/` response is not a JSON list, the collector shall raise CollectorError `eod {SYM}: expected a JSON list`; otherwise it shall drop every row whose `close` is absent, null, zero or negative, keep the first row per `date` string, and return the surviving provider rows unmodified, sorted ascending by `date` string.

*Why:* close<=0 rows are provider glitch rows

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A bar endpoint answering something other than a JSON list fails the leg; collectors.feature: EODHD bars drop glitch rows, keep the first duplicate and sort by date

### JDL-033 · contract · basis both
The EODHD collector shall turn each `/splits/` entry `{date, split}` into a split event with date = `date`, ratio = new/old parsed from `split` as `NEW/OLD` floats (e.g. `4/1` -> 4.0, `3.000000/2.000000` -> 1.5), and the split string kept verbatim, returned sorted ascending by date (stable); an unparseable string shall raise ValueError `unparseable split string: {s!r}` and a zero side `degenerate split string: {s!r}`.

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A first sync writes both actions files in the documented envelope; collectors.feature: A split string that is not NEW/OLD fails the leg

### JDL-034 · contract · basis both
The EODHD collector shall return the `/div/` entries verbatim (every provider field kept), sorted ascending by their `date` string (a missing date sorts as the empty string).

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A first sync writes both actions files in the documented envelope; actions.feature: Dividends are stored verbatim in date order and splits may be absent

### JDL-035 · contract · basis both
The EODHD collector shall declare its volume basis `split_adjusted` (served volume is already forward split-adjusted while prices are raw) and the Binance collector shall declare `raw`; the declaration is consulted only when a series is stored with price_basis `raw`.

*Why:* measured at a live re-record: /eod/ prices arrive raw but volume arrives already split-adjusted

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Binance klines become pre-adjusted bars dated by their UTC open time

### JDL-036 · contract · basis both
The Binance collector shall call `GET https://api.binance.com/api/v3/klines` with params `symbol` (the universe symbol verbatim), `interval=1d`, `limit=1000`, `startTime` (only when a cursor exists) and `endTime` (only when an end is given), needs no key, and exposes its page limit (1000) as the collector attribute `limit`.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A first fill without a start that lands on the page limit says it is a trailing window; collectors.feature: Binance klines become pre-adjusted bars dated by their UTC open time

### JDL-039 · contract · basis both
The Binance collector shall map each kline array to the bar `{date: UTC date of element 0 (ms) as YYYY-MM-DD, open: float(e1), high: float(e2), low: float(e3), close: float(e4), adjusted_close: float(e4), volume: float(e5)}`, drop bars with close <= 0, keep the first bar per date, and return them sorted ascending by date; volume is in base-asset units.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Binance klines become pre-adjusted bars dated by their UTC open time

### JDL-040 · contract · basis both
The corporate-actions store shall keep one JSON file per symbol and kind at `{store}/corporate_actions/splits/{SYMBOL}.json` and `{store}/corporate_actions/dividends/{SYMBOL}.json` (every `/` in the symbol replaced by `_`), each written with 2-space indentation plus a trailing newline and holding, in this key order, `symbol`, `exchange`, `last_updated` and `splits` or `dividends`.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A first sync writes both actions files in the documented envelope; store.feature: A sync and an import leave exactly the documented files

### JDL-041 · contract · basis logic
Each stored split item shall be `{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "split": the provider split string, "ratio": float}` (split string `{ratio:g}/1` when an event carries none), sorted ascending by date; reading splits back shall take `date` and `ratio` from the file (the stored ratio drives every calculation, the split string is never re-parsed).

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A first sync writes both actions files in the documented envelope; actions.feature: A stamp from the same UTC day skips the refresh and the stored splits are used; adjustment.feature: The adjust command re-derives the mains from raw with whatever splits are stored

### JDL-043 · contract · basis logic
The `last_updated` stamp shall be the real wall-clock UTC time at the moment the file is written, formatted as naive ISO 8601 plus `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` when microseconds are zero); an injected run clock never reaches the stamp.

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A first sync writes both actions files in the documented envelope; actions.feature: A later run on an earlier injected day finds the real-clock stamp fresh unless forced

### JDL-044 · contract · basis both
When a symbol's actions file is absent, reading it shall yield no events (an empty list) and no stamp (null); a stamp shall be read by replacing `Z` with `+00:00` and parsing ISO 8601, and its UTC calendar date is what every freshness rule compares.

*Why:* absent = no known actions, so symbols without splits don't force API calls

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A stamp from the same UTC day skips the refresh and the stored splits are used; collectors.feature: Binance klines become pre-adjusted bars dated by their UTC open time

### JDL-053 · contract · basis both
The price basis of a stored series shall be resolved from the provider and the DECLARED asset_type only, never from the symbol suffix: eodhd + asset_type crypto -> `split_adjusted`; eodhd + stock or etf -> `raw`; binance -> `split_adjusted`; yahoo-csv import -> `split_adjusted`; a `split_adjusted` series never receives split events.

*Why:* a declared crypto outside the .CC namespace stored raw would be put through the split pass - the double-adjustment class

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates; adjustment.feature: An EODHD crypto series is stored as served, end-guarded at the previous UTC day; adjustment.feature: An ETF with dividends and no splits is raw basis with factor 1 and dividends never applied; adjustment.feature: The declared class, never the .CC suffix, decides basis, actions and guard; decisions.feature: The provider and the declared class decide the basis and the actions part

### JDL-057 · contract · basis both
The market-data store shall keep each series under `{store}/market_data/exchange={exchange tag}/symbol={symbol}/` with one Parquet file per calendar year of the UTC session date at `year={YYYY}/data.parquet` (snappy compression), and a lock file `.lock` in the symbol directory created on the first write.

*Realised by:* component

### JDL-059 · contract · basis both
Every stored row shall carry exactly these 21 columns in this order and Parquet type: timestamp int64; datetime timestamp[ms, tz=UTC]; open, high, low, close, volume float64; symbol, exchange, asset_type, asset_subtype string; adjustment_factor, open_raw, high_raw, low_raw, close_raw, volume_raw, adjusted_close, cumulative_split_factor float64; currency, price_basis string.

### JDL-062 · contract · basis logic
When bars are stored, `symbol` shall be the store symbol, `exchange` the store partition tag (not the provider name), `asset_type` the declared store asset_type, `asset_subtype` the empty string, `currency` the leg's currency, and `price_basis` the resolved basis, identical on every row of the write.

### JDL-063 · contract · basis both
When a series is read, the store shall concatenate its year files in path order, sort rows by timestamp (stable), keep the first row of any duplicated timestamp, and number rows 0..n-1; a series with no year file shall read as a zero-row frame with the 21 columns.

*Realised by:* series_state  
*Verified by:* store.feature: Every stored series reads back with the 21 columns in schema order

### JDL-064 · contract · basis both
The latest stored session of a series shall be the maximum UTC date in the lexicographically last `year=` file, or none when the series has no file; the newest-n stored sessions shall be the n most recent distinct UTC dates (all of them when fewer exist), ascending.

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* sync.feature: The tail window and the latest session read across year files

### JDL-067 · contract · basis logic
Each revised cell shall be reported as `{"date": served row's UTC date YYYY-MM-DD, "column": as-served column name, "stored": float, "served": float}`, ordered by served row order and, within a row, in the column order open_raw, high_raw, low_raw, close_raw, volume_raw, adjusted_close; `served` is the value as it would be stored (after volume raw-ization).

*Realised by:* data_model, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* store.feature: Rows a provider serves outside the requested window are reconciled too; store.feature: The tail refresh reconciles newest-wins inside the window and keeps older history frozen

### JDL-068 · contract · basis logic
The reconcile shall report as its bar count the number of served bars handed to it (re-served unchanged rows included), shall write nothing when no row is replaced and none is new, shall write only the year files of replaced or new rows otherwise, and shall write every served row (no revisions) when the series is empty.

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* store.feature: An unchanged re-serve of pre-split rows produces no phantom revision; store.feature: The tail refresh reconciles newest-wins inside the window and keeps older history frozen

### JDL-071 · contract · basis both
The exported frame shall have exactly the columns Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close, Volume, one row per stored row in stored order, with Date = the UTC date of `datetime` as `YYYY-MM-DD` text, Open/High/Low/Close = the adjusted main columns, Adj Close = `adjusted_close`, all float64.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Exporting the two-split equity writes the adjusted mains with a float Volume

### JDL-073 · contract · basis both
The export shall pass every stored row through, zero-volume and NaN rows included, and shall apply no load policy of its own.

*Why:* the seam owns the zero-volume/NaN drop policy

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: The export passes zero-volume rows through and the report announces the seam's drop

### JDL-074 · contract · basis prose
The downstream seam that consumes the exported frame (outside this program) applies the load policy the validation notes announce: it sorts by date, drops rows whose Date does not parse, drops zero-volume rows and drops rows with a NaN in any column; this program implements that policy nowhere except where status emulates the zero-volume and NaN drop (JDL-122, JDL-120).

*Realised by:* component, status_run  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: The export passes zero-volume rows through and the report announces the seam's drop

### JDL-076 · contract · basis logic
When a frame is validated, a missing required column (Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close, Volume) shall produce the single error `missing required columns: {list}` and stop; extra columns shall produce the note `extra columns {list} are carried through; NaNs in them will drop rows at load (the transform drops any-NaN rows)`.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Findings that stop the validation early; seam.feature: Shape, numeric and date findings, errors before notes

### JDL-077 · contract · basis logic
When a frame is validated, a price column (Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close) or Volume shall be non-numeric when numeric coercion yields more missing values than the column already had, producing one error `non-numeric values in {list}` for all such columns; the negative, High<Low, zero-volume, NaN-row and clean-row checks run only when no column is non-numeric.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Shape, numeric and date findings, errors before notes

### JDL-078 · contract · basis logic
When a frame is validated, Date values that do not parse shall produce the error `no parseable dates in 'Date'` (and stop) when none parses, else the note `{n} unparseable date(s) - those rows drop at load`; duplicated parsed dates shall produce the error `{n} duplicate date(s) - forbidden by the contract`; non-ascending parsed dates shall produce the note `dates not sorted ascending - the load transform sorts`.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Findings that stop the validation early; seam.feature: Shape, numeric and date findings, errors before notes; seam.feature: The export passes zero-volume rows through and the report announces the seam's drop

### JDL-079 · contract · basis logic
When a frame is validated with all columns numeric, it shall add the errors `negative prices in {columns}`, `negative values in Volume` and `{n} row(s) with High < Low`, and the notes `{n} zero-volume row(s) - dropped at load by policy`, `{n} row(s) with NaN - dropped at load` (NaN in any required column) and `{clean} clean row(s) < recommended minimum {min} (720 warm-up + 395 lags) - the default counter window needs more history (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §1)`, where clean counts rows with a parsed date, non-zero volume and no NaN among the six numeric columns.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Exporting the two-split equity writes the adjusted mains with a float Volume; seam.feature: The export passes zero-volume rows through and the report announces the seam's drop; seam.feature: Value findings when every column is numeric

### JDL-081 · contract · basis logic
The validation report shall render as one line `ERROR: {error}` per error, then one line `note:  {note}` (two spaces) per note, each list in the order the checks run, or the single line `contract: clean`; the report is ok exactly when it holds no error.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment, data_model  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Exporting the two-split equity writes the adjusted mains with a float Volume; seam.feature: Shape, numeric and date findings, errors before notes; seam.feature: Validating a clean CSV, with and without enough history

### JDL-105 · contract · basis logic
The plan description of a leg shall be `{asset:>6} {exchange}/{symbol}: import {path} (whole file, idempotent)` for yahoo-csv, else `{asset:>6} {exchange}/{symbol}: {action} ({window})` with action `sync-actions + load` (actions-eligible) or `load`, window `reconcile tail of {tail} session(s) from {start}` (stored rows), `first fill from {start}` (start declared) or `first fill, full history`, then ` to {end}` when an end applies and ` - INVERTED: end predates the stored tail, nothing to fetch` when stored rows exist and start > end.
