## Arithmetic: adjustment, factors, measurements (22)

### JDL-031 · arithmetic · basis both
The EODHD symbol normaliser shall pass a symbol containing `.` through unchanged; map `BASE/QUOTE` to `{BASE}{QUOTE}.FOREX` (upper-cased) when both sides are in the fiat set (USD EUR GBP JPY CHF AUD NZD CAD SEK NOK DKK PLN CZK HUF TRY ZAR MXN SGD HKD CNY INR BRL KRW RUB), else to `{BASE}-{QUOTE}.CC` when QUOTE is in the crypto-quote set (USD USDT EUR BTC ETH BUSD USDC), else raise CollectorError `cannot infer exchange for pair symbol {symbol!r}`; any other bare ticker gains `.US`.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: The hand-run load normalises the symbol and refuses a declaration it cannot trust; collectors.feature: Unwrapped collector errors of the hand-run EODHD commands

### JDL-037 · arithmetic · basis logic
The Binance collector shall convert a start date to `startTime` = Unix milliseconds of that date at 00:00 UTC and an end date to `endTime` = Unix milliseconds of that date at 00:00 UTC + 86 400 000 - 1.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Binance klines become pre-adjusted bars dated by their UTC open time

### JDL-045 · arithmetic · basis both
The cumulative split factor of a row shall be computed in float64 starting from 1.0 and multiplying, for each split event in stored (ascending-date) order, by that event's ratio when the row's UTC calendar date is strictly before the event's date.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates

### JDL-046 · arithmetic · basis both
A row dated on a split's effective date shall not include that split in its factor (it already trades at the new basis), so the first row of a series older than every split carries the product of all ratios.

*Why:* the effective date is the first session at the new price basis

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates

### JDL-047 · arithmetic · basis both
When a series is adjusted, each of open, high, low and close shall be set to its `*_raw` value divided by the row's factor (float64 division), and `cumulative_split_factor` shall be set to the factor.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates

### JDL-048 · arithmetic · basis both
When a series is adjusted, volume shall be set to `volume_raw` multiplied by the row's factor (float64), so a volume whose raw-ization is not exactly invertible stays non-integral (e.g. 100000 / 10.5 * 10.5 = 99999.99999999999).

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates

### JDL-049 · arithmetic · basis both
The adjustment shall read only the `*_raw` columns and the split events, carry every other column unchanged, and return a new frame, so adjusting an already adjusted series with the same events is a fixed point and re-adjusting after the event list changes re-derives every main column from raw.

*Why:* the NJAPMP pass divided the stored main columns in place on every run, compounding corruption; a pure function of raw + events makes that unrepresentable and doubles as the repair path

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment, series_state  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A split synced after the first fill re-derives every price but only re-raw-izes the tail's volume; adjustment.feature: The adjust command re-derives the mains from raw with whatever splits are stored

### JDL-050 · arithmetic · basis both
Dividends shall never enter any price, volume or factor calculation (split-only policy); they are stored and never applied.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: An ETF with dividends and no splits is raw basis with factor 1 and dividends never applied

### JDL-054 · arithmetic · basis both
When bars are stored with price_basis `raw` from a collector whose volume basis is `split_adjusted`, the program shall set `volume_raw` = served volume / factor computed from the splits known at ingest (float64 division) and then derive volume = volume_raw * factor per the adjustment; with volume basis `raw`, `volume_raw` = served volume; any other volume basis value shall raise StoreError `unknown volume_basis {value!r}`.

*Why:* true raw is split-invariant, so a split synced later repairs through re-adjustment exactly like prices; the flip side is that splits must be synced before the first load of a split-history symbol

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A split synced after the first fill re-derives every price but only re-raw-izes the tail's volume; adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates; store.feature: An unchanged re-serve of pre-split rows produces no phantom revision

### JDL-055 · arithmetic · basis both
When bars are stored with price_basis `split_adjusted`, each main column (open, high, low, close, volume) and its `*_raw` twin shall both hold the served value and `cumulative_split_factor` shall be 1.0.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: An EODHD crypto series is stored as served, end-guarded at the previous UTC day; decisions.feature: The provider and the declared class decide the basis and the actions part; decisions.feature: volume_raw is raw-ized only for EODHD raw-basis series

### JDL-056 · arithmetic · basis both
When a bar is stored, `adjusted_close` shall be the bar's `adjusted_close` value whenever the bar carries that key (a NaN value stays NaN), else its `close` (for Yahoo CSVs the `Adj Close` column, always carried), and `adjustment_factor` shall be adjusted_close / close_raw (float64).

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates; adjustment.feature: An ETF with dividends and no splits is raw basis with factor 1 and dividends never applied; decisions.feature: volume_raw is raw-ized only for EODHD raw-basis series

### JDL-060 · arithmetic · basis logic
When bars are stored, each bar's `date` string shall be parsed as a UTC instant (format inferred from the first bar; a date-only string gives that day's 00:00 UTC, a time of day if present is kept, never truncated); `datetime` shall hold it at millisecond resolution, and `timestamp` shall hold the Unix epoch in whole SECONDS (e.g. 2024-01-02 -> 1704153600) - the value the pinned environment produces for date-only strings, despite the column being documented as milliseconds.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A two-split equity is stored raw and adjusted around both effective dates

### JDL-072 · arithmetic · basis both
The exported Volume column shall be int64 when the series is non-empty and every volume is finite and integral, and float64 (values unchanged) otherwise - a single non-integral or NaN volume makes the whole column float64.

*Why:* mirrors pd.read_csv's inference so the seam is bit-exact against a CSV load of the same data

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Exporting a series whose volumes are all integral writes an int64 Volume; seam.feature: Exporting the two-split equity writes the adjusted mains with a float Volume

### JDL-080 · arithmetic · basis both
The recommended minimum clean-row count shall be 1115 (720 warm-up rows + 30 offset + 365 period), overridable by `validate --min-rows`; the clean-row note appears only when clean < minimum.

*Why:* 720 warm-up rows before the first counter + offset 30 + period 365 forward lags consumed by the feature block

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Validating a clean CSV, with and without enough history

### JDL-082 · arithmetic · basis both
The differential shall align the two frames on identical Date strings (each sorted by Date) and, for Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close and Volume over the common dates, compute rel = |a - b| / max(|a|, |b|) with a zero denominator replaced by 1.0, rel = 0 when both values are NaN and rel = infinity when exactly one is; a cell is beyond tolerance when rel > tolerance (default 1e-4).

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: The store commands on a filled raw-basis series; differential.feature: A stored series against a CSV with one changed cell and unmatched dates; differential.feature: Two stored series that agree are aligned within tolerance

### JDL-093 · arithmetic · basis both
The fetch start of a collector leg shall be the universe `start` (or none) while the series has no stored row, and otherwise the oldest of the newest `tail` stored sessions (the tail-refresh window), as `YYYY-MM-DD`; the universe `start` is never read again once the series has rows.

*Why:* start is a first-fill floor only

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A collector leg first-fills an absent series; decisions.feature: A collector leg tail-refreshes a filled series; decisions.feature: A filled series starts at the oldest of its newest tail sessions; decisions.feature: A filled series with a well-ordered window sends its request; decisions.feature: The first fill starts at the universe start, or is open; store.feature: The tail refresh reconciles newest-wins inside the window and keeps older history frozen; sync.feature: The tail window and the latest session read across year files; sync.feature: The tail window starts at the oldest of the newest N stored sessions

### JDL-094 · arithmetic · basis both
The fetch end of a collector leg shall be the earlier (ISO string minimum) of the universe `end` and, for a leg whose DECLARED asset_type is crypto (any provider), the end-guard `today - 1 day`; with neither, the fetch is open-ended; the universe `end` caps every fetch, first fill and tail refresh alike.

*Why:* the provider serves the in-progress UTC day; the guard keys on the declared class because a union of provider and suffix tests silently lost the guard for a crypto leg matching neither

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: An EODHD crypto series is stored as served, end-guarded at the previous UTC day; adjustment.feature: The declared class, never the .CC suffix, decides basis, actions and guard; decisions.feature: The fetch end is the ISO minimum of the universe end and the crypto end-guard; sync.feature: A dry run plans every leg shape from local state only; sync.feature: A universe end caps the first fill, and wins the minimum against the crypto end-guard

### JDL-115 · arithmetic · basis both
The expected sessions between two dates shall be the calendar days strictly after the first and strictly before the second, keeping only Monday-Friday for asset_type `stock` or `etf` and every day for any other asset_type (crypto); there is no holiday calendar.

*Why:* today's bar may legitimately not exist yet; single-day market holidays stay under the default threshold - the conscious no-calendar decision

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Corporate-actions freshness counts the refresh sessions missed since the stamp; status.feature: Crypto staleness counts every calendar day; status.feature: The largest post-seam gap is counted in expected sessions and noted at the threshold; status.feature: Weekday staleness counts the sessions strictly between the last bar and today

### JDL-119 · arithmetic · basis both
The longest zero-volume run shall be counted by row position in stored order (never by calendar days), and among equally long runs the earliest shall be reported, with the UTC dates of its first and last rows.

*Why:* consecutive stored rows are exactly what the seam drops together

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Zero-volume rows are noted, with the longest contiguous run when it exceeds one row

### JDL-120 · arithmetic · basis both
The post-seam gap shall be measured over the surviving rows (volume > 0 and close not NaN) in stored order: for each consecutive pair more than one calendar day apart, the number of expected sessions strictly between them; the largest such count (earliest on ties) with its two dates, or none when every count is 0.

*Why:* zero-volume drops and provider-omitted rows read identically here, which is the point

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: The largest post-seam gap is counted in expected sessions and noted at the threshold

### JDL-122 · arithmetic · basis both
The price-resolution measurement shall take the `close_raw` values of rows with volume > 0, drop NaN and non-positive values, keep the newest `--resolution-window` (default 500) of them in stored order (falling back to `close` when that leaves nothing), and when fewer than 60 remain report nothing; otherwise sessions = count, distinct = number of distinct values, min_tick = the smallest (d[k+1] - d[k]) / d[k] over the sorted distinct values (null when only one), flat_share = (consecutive equal pairs) / (sessions - 1).

*Why:* measured on close_raw, the provider's own print: the split pass manufactures decimals that were never quoted; below 60 sessions the ratio is noise

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Price resolution is measured over traded sessions and noted past its knobs; status.feature: Resolution needs at least 60 traded sessions in its window; status.feature: Resolution reads the provider's own print, not the split-adjusted close

### JDL-128 · arithmetic · basis both
The common session of a pair shall be the latest UTC date present in both series' last `--window` stored rows; each side's close is the adjusted `close` of its last stored row on that date; spread = |close_a - close_b| / ((close_a + close_b) / 2), measured whenever the mid is non-zero.

*Why:* bounded by the window on purpose: pairing today's close against an ancient one would measure drift

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: The cross-venue close spread warns strictly above its threshold, or alerts when promoted; status.feature: The spread needs a common session inside both newest windows and a non-zero mid

## Rituals: the sync, its legs, windows and gates (27)

### JDL-027 · ritual · basis both
When a collector request answers HTTP 429 or any status >= 500, or the transport raises a connection error, the collector shall retry up to 4 times (5 attempts in all), sleeping `2.0 * 2**attempt` seconds after attempt 0, 1, 2, 3, and shall acquire the rate limiter before every attempt.

*Why:* retries and rate limiting live in the collector, not the transport, so they are exercised identically for live and replayed traffic

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A 503 is retried five times, then the leg fails before any bar is fetched

### JDL-038 · ritual · basis both
The Binance collector shall page ascending: the first page uses startTime = start (omitted without a start); a page ends the loop when it is empty, holds fewer rows than `limit`, or its last openTime + one day in milliseconds (the day length of JDL-037) exceeds endTime; otherwise the next page's startTime is the last openTime + one day; more than 100 pages shall raise CollectorError `pagination exceeded 100 pages - refusing to truncate silently; raise max_pages if the range is real`; a non-list page shall raise CollectorError `klines {symbol}: expected a JSON list`.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A bar endpoint answering something other than a JSON list fails the leg; collectors.feature: Binance pages ascending from the declared start until a short page

### JDL-042 · ritual · basis both
When corporate actions are synced for a symbol, the program shall fetch splits, then dividends, then write the splits file, then the dividends file, each with exchange `eodhd` and the same kind of stamp, and report the two counts; the writes are plain truncating writes (not atomic).

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A first sync writes both actions files in the documented envelope; actions.feature: Dividends are stored verbatim in date order and splits may be absent; collectors.feature: A 404 on the bars fails the leg after the corporate actions were refreshed

### JDL-058 · ritual · basis both
When a year file is written, the store shall write `data.parquet.tmp` beside it and atomically rename it over `data.parquet`, remove any leftover `*.tmp` year files of that series before writing, and, when pruning, delete stale year files only after every new file is in place; every read-modify-write of a series shall hold an exclusive advisory lock on its `.lock` file, waiting up to 300 s polling every 0.5 s and then raising StoreError `{exchange}/{symbol}: another writer holds the store lock after 300s ({lock path})`.

*Why:* a reader never sees a torn file and no instant exists where raw history is only in memory; a stuck lock holder must be surfaced, never silently queued behind

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* store.feature: A sync and an import leave exactly the documented files

### JDL-065 · ritual · basis both
When served bars are reconciled into a series, the store shall compare each served row whose timestamp is already stored on the six as-served columns open_raw, high_raw, low_raw, close_raw, volume_raw, adjusted_close (exact equality, two NaNs equal), replace the stored row wholesale when any differs, keep the stored row untouched when none differs, append served rows with new timestamps, and never touch stored rows the served set does not contain; derived columns are not compared.

*Why:* derived columns re-derive from the as-served ones and are excluded on purpose; raw-ization makes a re-served pre-split bar comparable, so an unchanged serve produces zero phantom revisions

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A split synced after the first fill re-derives every price but only re-raw-izes the tail's volume; decisions.feature: A collector leg tail-refreshes a filled series; store.feature: An unchanged re-serve of pre-split rows produces no phantom revision; store.feature: The tail refresh reconciles newest-wins inside the window and keeps older history frozen

### JDL-066 · ritual · basis both
The reconcile shall consider every timestamp it is handed, including served rows older than the requested window: frozen-first-seen history outside the tail is enforced only by the fetch window, never by the store.

*Why:* this method only ever considers the timestamps it is handed

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* store.feature: Rows a provider serves outside the requested window are reconciled too

### JDL-069 · ritual · basis both
When a raw-basis series is re-adjusted, the store shall, under the series lock, read the whole series, re-derive it through the adjustment with the given split events, rewrite every year file (pruning stale ones) only when any value changed, and report the row count; an empty series shall raise StoreError `nothing stored for {exchange}/{symbol}`.

*Why:* the daily no-new-bars case costs a read and a compare, never a rewrite

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A split synced after the first fill re-derives every price but only re-raw-izes the tail's volume; adjustment.feature: The adjust command re-derives the mains from raw with whatever splits are stored; adjustment.feature: The adjust command refuses what it must not adjust; decisions.feature: The store commands on a filled raw-basis series; decisions.feature: The store commands on an absent series; decisions.feature: Where an error is raised decides how the user sees it

### JDL-070 · ritual · basis both
When a Yahoo CSV is imported, the store shall require the columns Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Adj Close, Volume (else StoreError `{csv path}: not a 7-column Yahoo CSV, missing {list}`), map each CSV row to a bar (Adj Close -> adjusted_close), store every row - zero-volume and NaN rows included - with price_basis `split_adjusted` and volume basis `raw`, REPLACE the whole stored series (prune stale years), and report the number of CSV rows (duplicate dates are counted but only the first is stored).

*Why:* the load policy belongs to the seam, not the store

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_run  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: An import into a chosen exchange tag keeps the declared labels; decisions.feature: A CSV leg overwrites whatever is there; decisions.feature: A yahoo-csv leg is always split_adjusted; decisions.feature: import-csv overwrites, whatever the store held; store.feature: A Yahoo CSV import replaces the whole series and reports the CSV row count; store.feature: An import refuses what it cannot store; sync.feature: A committed CSV leg imports its whole file without any collector

### JDL-084 · ritual · basis both
The sync and status commands shall select legs as every enabled asset (universe order) x every enabled source of it (source order), keeping only assets named by the asset filter and sources whose provider is in the provider filter when those filters are given; each leg carries the keys and derivations of contracts/leg.md.

*Realised by:* data_model, sync_run  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: The declared class, never the .CC suffix, decides basis, actions and guard; sync.feature: Asset and provider filters keep universe order and skip paused assets and switched-off sources; sync.feature: The packaged universe expands into nine ordered legs

### JDL-086 · ritual · basis both
A leg shall be actions-eligible exactly when its provider is `eodhd` and its DECLARED asset_type is not `crypto`, whatever the symbol suffix (a `.CC` symbol declared stock is eligible; an EODHD symbol outside `.CC` declared crypto is not).

*Why:* eligibility reads the declared class, like the end-guard and the basis; a .CC symbol declared non-crypto is a mis-declaration whose fix is the declaration

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: The declared class, never the .CC suffix, decides basis, actions and guard; collectors.feature: Binance klines become pre-adjusted bars dated by their UTC open time; decisions.feature: A leg that is not actions-eligible has no actions part; decisions.feature: A same-day stored split excuses the jump of an actions-eligible leg; decisions.feature: Only actions-eligible legs are checked; the stamp's age decides; decisions.feature: The provider and the declared class decide the basis and the actions part; status.feature: A same-day split excuses a jump only where splits are read; sync.feature: The packaged universe expands into nine ordered legs

### JDL-088 · ritual · basis both
The sync shall take `today` as the UTC calendar date of the run clock (the real current UTC time unless a clock is injected) once at the start of the run, and use it for the crypto end-guard, the actions gate and the today-dated-bar check of every leg.

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* sync.feature: A universe end caps the first fill, and wins the minimum against the crypto end-guard; sync.feature: An equity bar dated on the run's UTC day is ingested and flagged

### JDL-090 · ritual · basis both
For an actions-eligible leg, the sync shall run, in this order: the actions gate and (when due) the corporate-actions sync; reading the stored splits; the bar fetch; the reconcile; the re-adjustment; so a failure of the bar fetch leaves the refreshed actions files in place, and a failure of the actions sync fetches no bars.

*Why:* for raw-basis EODHD series the order (sync-actions BEFORE load) is load-bearing for volume raw-ization

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A 404 on the bars fails the leg after the corporate actions were refreshed; collectors.feature: A 503 is retried five times, then the leg fails before any bar is fetched; collectors.feature: When both the actions and the bars would fail, the actions failure is what the leg reports

### JDL-091 · ritual · basis both
The actions gate shall refresh an actions-eligible leg's corporate actions when force-actions is set, or no splits stamp exists, or the stamp's UTC date is earlier than `today`; otherwise it shall skip the refresh and contribute `actions fresh; ` to the leg detail.

*Why:* a calendar date cannot be missed by a second; a run straddling midnight UTC stamps tomorrow and skips one refresh, absorbed by the status side's two-session tolerance

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A later run on an earlier injected day finds the real-clock stamp fresh unless forced; actions.feature: A stamp from an earlier UTC day refreshes, a second before midnight or not; actions.feature: A stamp from the same UTC day skips the refresh and the stored splits are used; decisions.feature: A stamp from an earlier UTC day refreshes, one from today or later skips; decisions.feature: No stamp means refresh; decisions.feature: force-actions refreshes whatever the stamp says

### JDL-092 · ritual · basis logic
An actions-eligible leg shall reconcile and re-adjust with the split events read from the actions store after the gate; every other leg shall use no split events.

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* actions.feature: A stamp from the same UTC day skips the refresh and the stored splits are used

### JDL-095 · ritual · basis both
When a leg's series has stored rows and its fetch start is later than its fetch end, the sync shall send no bar request, treat the fetch as zero bars, keep the leg green, and add `end {end} predates the stored tail (from {start}); nothing fetched - a pinned window with rows past its end, the fix is the declaration; ` to the detail; an empty series with start > end still sends its request.

*Why:* a provider's answer to from > to is undefined; never red, the fix is the declaration

*Realised by:* series_state, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A filled series whose end predates its tail sends no request and stays green; decisions.feature: An empty series sends its request even when the end-guard falls before the declared start; sync.feature: A series with rows past its declared end fetches nothing and stays green

### JDL-096 · ritual · basis both
When a first fill (no stored row) of a leg with no universe `start` receives exactly as many bars as the collector's `limit` attribute (Binance's page limit of JDL-036; the EODHD collector has none), the sync shall keep the bars and add `first fill hit the provider page limit ({n} bars, no start declared) - the series is a trailing window, not history; ` to the detail.

*Why:* a first fill that lands exactly on the page limit is the provider's default slice, not history

*Realised by:* series_state  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A first fill without a start that lands on the page limit says it is a trailing window

### JDL-097 · ritual · basis both
After the reconcile of a leg whose basis is `raw`, the sync shall re-adjust the whole stored series with the leg's split events whenever the series has at least one stored row (also when zero bars were fetched); split_adjusted legs are never re-adjusted.

*Why:* gated on the basis, not on actions eligibility; re-adjustment refuses a split_adjusted series by design

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A split synced after the first fill re-derives every price but only re-raw-izes the tail's volume; sync.feature: A series with rows past its declared end fetches nothing and stays green

### JDL-098 · ritual · basis both
The detail of a successful collector leg shall be the concatenation of: the actions part (`{s} split(s), {d} dividend(s); ` after a refresh, `actions fresh; ` after a skipped one, nothing for other legs), the inverted-window part, the page-limit part, `{bars} bar(s), {r} revised cell(s)` (bars = number of bars handed to the reconcile), and `; today-dated bar ingested (pre-close fetch?)` when the newest fetched bar is dated `today`.

*Realised by:* sync_leg  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A leg that is not actions-eligible has no actions part; store.feature: The tail refresh reconciles newest-wins inside the window and keeps older history frozen; sync.feature: A universe end caps the first fill, and wins the minimum against the crypto end-guard; sync.feature: An equity bar dated on the run's UTC day is ingested and flagged; sync.feature: The summary carries every revision as plain numbers

### JDL-099 · ritual · basis both
A yahoo-csv leg shall import its whole CSV file (path as declared, relative to the working directory) as an overwrite of its store series per JDL-070, with the leg's asset_type and currency, contacting no collector, and its detail shall be `{rows} row(s) imported`.

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Without an EODHD key every EODHD leg fails and the CSV leg still lands; decisions.feature: A CSV leg overwrites whatever is there; decisions.feature: A yahoo-csv leg is always split_adjusted; sync.feature: A committed CSV leg imports its whole file without any collector; sync.feature: A committed CSV leg whose file is missing fails that leg alone

### JDL-100 · ritual · basis both
A binance leg shall never sync corporate actions and shall store price_basis `split_adjusted` with volume basis `raw`, whatever its asset's declared class; whether it is end-guarded follows JDL-094 (the declared class).

*Realised by:* series_state  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Binance klines become pre-adjusted bars dated by their UTC open time; decisions.feature: The provider and the declared class decide the basis and the actions part

### JDL-101 · ritual · basis both
When any exception escapes a leg, the sync shall record that leg as failed with detail `{exception class name}: {exception message}` and no revisions, and continue with the next leg; a run is ok exactly when no leg failed, and revisions never fail a run.

*Why:* a batch that half-succeeds must never look green

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A degenerate stored split ratio fails the leg before anything is written; collectors.feature: A request no fixture answers fails the leg and names what is known; collectors.feature: Without an EODHD key every EODHD leg fails and the CSV leg still lands; decisions.feature: An error inside a leg fails that leg only; sync.feature: A committed CSV leg whose file is missing fails that leg alone; sync.feature: One failing leg does not stop the others and the run turns red

### JDL-102 · ritual · basis both
The sync shall construct a collector only when a non-dry-run leg first needs that provider, at most once per provider per run (an injected collector is always used instead), shall construct the EODHD collector with the `--base-url` override when given, and shall close every collector it constructed after the last leg; a failed EODHD construction (no key) fails each eodhd leg in turn without affecting other legs.

*Why:* a CSV-only or --dry-run invocation demands no key

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Without an EODHD key every EODHD leg fails and the CSV leg still lands; sync.feature: One failing leg does not stop the others and the run turns red

### JDL-103 · ritual · basis both
The sync shall emit one log line per leg, `ok      {asset} {exchange}/{symbol} [{provider}]: {detail}` or `FAILED  {asset} {exchange}/{symbol} [{provider}]: {detail}`; after an ok line, one line `        revised {date} {column}: {stored:g} -> {served:g}` for each of the first 10 revisions and `        ... {k} more revised cell(s)` when k = count - 10 > 0; and finally `{legs} leg(s), {failed} failed -> store {store path!r}`.

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Without an EODHD key every EODHD leg fails and the CSV leg still lands; decisions.feature: An error inside a leg fails that leg only; store.feature: The run log echoes the first ten revisions and counts the rest; store.feature: The tail refresh reconciles newest-wins inside the window and keeps older history frozen; sync.feature: One failing leg does not stop the others and the run turns red

### JDL-104 · ritual · basis both
When the sync runs as a dry run, it shall construct no collector, contact no provider and write nothing, emit `plan for store {store path!r} ({n} leg(s)):` then one line per leg of two spaces plus the plan description of JDL-105, and return every leg as ok with detail `planned` and the run ok.

*Why:* plans from local store state, so it needs neither network nor key

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: The first fill starts at the universe start, or is open; sync.feature: A dry run plans every leg shape from local state only; sync.feature: A series with rows past its declared end fetches nothing and stays green; sync.feature: The CLI dry run uses the universe's default store and still writes the summary

### JDL-107 · ritual · basis both
The status command shall check, in leg order, every selected leg whose provider is not `yahoo-csv` (committed CSV snapshots are not a live feed), and then, for every asset with two or more such legs (in first-appearance order), every leg pair (i, j) with i < j in leg order.

*Why:* committed CSV snapshots are not a live feed - nothing to check

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Never-filled series and the declared-class verdicts against the packaged evidence; status.feature: The cross-venue close spread warns strictly above its threshold, or alerts when promoted; status.feature: The status table of a pair and of a CSV-only selection

### JDL-108 · ritual · basis both
The status checks shall take `today` as the UTC calendar date of the real current time (the harness may inject a clock), and shall read the store and the actions store only - no key, no network, no writes.

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Weekday staleness counts the sessions strictly between the last bar and today

### JDL-110 · ritual · basis logic
The source checks shall append their messages in this order: declared class; never filled (which ends the report); staleness; today-dated; zero volume; post-seam continuity; price resolution; phantom jumps (ascending date); corporate-actions freshness.

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: Status on an absent and on a filled series; status.feature: A class disagreement on a healthy series warns without failing the day

## Verdicts: what status reports and how (12)

### JDL-111 · verdict · basis both
For an eodhd leg only, the status command shall compare the leg's declared asset_type with the packaged vendor evidence (contracts/classifications.toml, keyed by exchange tag + symbol) and set `declared_class_check` to the verdict; a `disagree` verdict shall add the WARNING `declared class: {message}` and every other verdict the NOTE `declared class: {message}`; neither ever alerts or changes the exit code.

*Why:* an alert here would stop every asset's publish over a metadata disagreement; binance and yahoo-csv have no classification endpoint, so a note would read as absent evidence rather than inapplicable

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: A class disagreement on a healthy series warns without failing the day; status.feature: Never-filled series and the declared-class verdicts against the packaged evidence

### JDL-112 · verdict · basis both
The declared-class verdict shall be: `no_evidence` with message `no vendor classification recorded - run tools/record_classifications.py` when no row exists; `not_comparable` with `vendor type {vt!r} cannot confirm asset_type {at!r}{seen}: the .CC (crypto) and .FOREX namespaces both serve it, so only the symbol's own namespace separates them and the evidence is not independent` for vendor type `Currency`; `unmapped` with `vendor type {vt!r} has no store asset_type counterpart{seen} - no verdict rather than a guess (mapped: ['Common Stock', 'ETF'])` for any other type outside the map; `agree` with `vendor type {vt!r} agrees with declared asset_type {at!r}{seen}` when the mapped type (Common Stock -> stock, ETF -> etf) equals the declaration; else `disagree` with `declared asset_type {at!r} but the vendor says {vt!r} (-> {mapped!r}){seen} for {exchange}/{symbol} - check the asset_class in universe.toml against docs/EVALUATION_ASSET_CLASSIFICATION.md §5 C2`; `{seen}` is `, recorded {last_verified}` when the row has a last_verified date, else empty.

*Why:* UNKNOWN is preferable to an incorrect class; Currency is shared by the .CC and .FOREX namespaces, so it confirms nothing

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Never-filled series and the declared-class verdicts against the packaged evidence

### JDL-114 · verdict · basis both
When a checked leg's series has no stored row, the status command shall add the ALERT `never filled - no stored rows (jef-data sync first)` and finish that report with no further field or check.

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A never-filled series alerts and its report ends there; decisions.feature: Status on an absent and on a filled series; status.feature: Never-filled series and the declared-class verdicts against the packaged evidence

### JDL-116 · verdict · basis both
When the expected sessions between the last stored session and today number at least the staleness threshold (`--staleness`, default 2), the status command shall add the ALERT `stale: {n} expected session(s) missing since {last} (multi-day holidays can trip this - verify before acting)`; `missed_sessions` reports n regardless.

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: Missed sessions below the threshold pass, at it alert; status.feature: Crypto staleness counts every calendar day; status.feature: Weekday staleness counts the sessions strictly between the last bar and today

### JDL-117 · verdict · basis both
When the last stored session equals today, the status command shall add the NOTE `today-dated bar stored (pre-close serve? the next tail-refresh heals it)`.

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Weekday staleness counts the sessions strictly between the last bar and today

### JDL-118 · verdict · basis both
When the stored series holds n > 0 rows with volume exactly 0, the status command shall add the NOTE `{n} zero-volume row(s), dropped at the seam by pinned policy`, extended by ` - largest contiguous run {length}, {first}..{last}` when the longest run of consecutive zero-volume rows is longer than 1 row.

*Why:* a run is a splice the model receives and a flat total cannot express it; scattered singles are not

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Zero-volume rows are noted, with the longest contiguous run when it exceeds one row

### JDL-121 · verdict · basis both
When the post-seam gap is at least the gap threshold (`--gap-k`, default 5), the status command shall add the NOTE `post-seam continuity: {n} expected session(s) absent between {prev} and {next} - the seam's output splices across this hole; verify the provider era before modelling (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §1)`; it never alerts.

*Why:* gap_k=5 is calibrated: the largest true US closure since 1962 measures 4 expected sessions; a hole is a property of the series, not of today's run

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: The largest post-seam gap is counted in expected sessions and noted at the threshold

### JDL-123 · verdict · basis both
When resolution was measured and distinct / sessions < `--resolution-k` (default 0.20) or flat_share > `--flat-k` (default 0.25), the status command shall add the NOTE `coarse price resolution: {distinct} distinct close(s) in {sessions} traded session(s), min tick {tick}, {flat_share:.1%} flat - the provider's quoting grid, verify before modelling (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §7.8)` with tick `{min_tick:.4%}` or `n/a`; it never alerts.

*Why:* coarse quoting is a property of an instrument, not a failure of today's run

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: Price resolution is measured over traded sessions and noted past its knobs; status.feature: Resolution reads the provider's own print, not the split-adjusted close

### JDL-124 · verdict · basis both
For each stored row index i from max(1, n - window) to n - 1 (window = `--window`, default 10) whose previous adjusted close is non-zero, the status command shall compute move = close[i] / close[i-1] - 1.0 and, when |move| > `--jump-threshold` (default 0.40, strict) and row i's UTC date is not the date of a stored split (splits are read only for actions-eligible legs), add the ALERT `phantom-split-shaped jump {move:+.1%} on {date} with no same-day split event - check corporate actions (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §2)`.

*Why:* the catastrophic input failure for the model is a missed split entering as a crash; this check confirms the preventive machinery worked

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A same-day stored split excuses the jump of an actions-eligible leg; decisions.feature: A zero previous close is skipped; the threshold is strict; an unexplained jump alerts; status.feature: A same-day split excuses a jump only where splits are read; status.feature: Phantom-split jumps are scanned over the newest window with a strict threshold

### JDL-125 · verdict · basis both
For an actions-eligible leg, the status command shall add the ALERT `corporate actions stale: never synced - run jef-data sync` when no splits stamp exists, and the ALERT `corporate actions stale: {n} refresh session(s) missed since {stamp date} - run jef-data sync` when the expected sessions strictly between the stamp's UTC date and today number at least 2 (fixed; not a command option).

*Why:* counted in refresh sessions, not wall-clock days, because the refresh rides the weekday leg; both sides are day-quantised so sync and status cannot disagree within a run

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: Only actions-eligible legs are checked; the stamp's age decides; decisions.feature: Refresh sessions missed since the stamp, below and at the fixed threshold of 2; status.feature: A same-day split excuses a jump only where splits are read; status.feature: An actions-eligible series that never synced its actions alerts at any threshold; status.feature: Corporate-actions freshness counts the refresh sessions missed since the stamp

### JDL-127 · verdict · basis both
When a pair cannot be measured, the status command shall add exactly one NOTE and leave common_session and spread null: `{label} has no stored rows - spread not measured` (first empty side, a then b); `no common session in the newest {window} - spread not measured (see the staleness check)`; or `zero mid price on {date} - spread not measured`.

*Why:* the per-source check already alerts never-filled; a second alert for the same fact would be noise

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A pair without a common session is not measured; status.feature: Never-filled series and the declared-class verdicts against the packaged evidence; status.feature: The spread needs a common session inside both newest windows and a non-zero mid

### JDL-129 · verdict · basis both
When a spread is measured, the status command shall always add the NOTE `close spread {spread:.4%} on {date} ({a} {close_a:g} vs {b} {close_b:g})`, and when spread > `--spread-threshold` (default 0.005, strict) also the finding `cross-venue close spread {spread:.4%} on {date} exceeds {threshold:.4%} ({a} {close_a:g} vs {b} {close_b:g}) - feed problem or venue distress; verify before acting, never trade it (docs/EVALUATION_CROSS_EXCHANGE.md)` as a WARNING, or as an ALERT when `--spread-alerts` is given.

*Why:* a breach compares a cross-check leg; an alert would stop the venue's whole day before it publishes, which a redundancy leg's disagreement does not warrant

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A measured spread is always noted, warns strictly above the threshold, alerts when promoted; status.feature: The cross-venue close spread warns strictly above its threshold, or alerts when promoted

## Refusals: every error the user can meet (21)

### JDL-012 · refusal · basis logic
The loader shall stop at the first violation, checking in this order: TOML syntax; top-level keys; `[defaults]` is a table; `[defaults]` keys; `store`; `currency`; `asset` is a non-empty array; then per asset in file order: is a table, keys, `name`, `asset_class` presence then value, `threshold`, `currency`, `source` non-empty array, `enabled`, then per source in order: is a table, keys, `provider` presence then value, `kind`, `symbol`, eodhd dot rule, `modeled`, `enabled`, `exchange`, `note`, `path`, `start`, `end`, CSV/collector key rules, start-after-end; then the asset's modeled rules; after all assets: duplicate names, then duplicate store coordinates.

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-013 · refusal · basis logic
If the universe text is not valid TOML, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{origin}: not valid TOML: {parser message}` where the parser message is Python `tomllib`'s exception text.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: Where an error is raised decides how the user sees it; universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-014 · refusal · basis logic
If a table carries a key outside its permitted set, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{where}: unknown key(s) {sorted unknown list}; allowed: {sorted allowed list}`, with `where` = `{origin}` (top level), `{origin} [defaults]`, `asset #{n}` (1-based, asset keys are checked before its name is known) or `asset '{name}' source #{n}`; lists render as Python lists of quoted strings.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-015 · refusal · basis logic
If the document's shape is wrong, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `{origin}: [defaults] must be a table`; `{origin}: no [[asset]] entries` (absent, empty or non-array `asset`); `asset #{n}: must be a table`; `asset '{name}': needs at least one [[asset.source]]` (absent, empty or non-array `source`); `asset '{name}' source #{n}: must be a table`.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-016 · refusal · basis logic
If a scalar is wrong, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `{where}: missing required key '{key}'`; `{where}: {key} must be a non-empty string, got {value!r}` (where is `[defaults]` for the defaults table); `{where}: {key} must be a boolean, got {value!r}` (enabled); `{where}: modeled must be a boolean, got {value!r}`; `{where}: threshold must be a number (documentation only), got {value!r}`; `{where}: {key} must be an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), got {value!r}`.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-017 · refusal · basis logic
If an enumerated value is unknown, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `asset '{name}': unknown asset_class {value!r}; allowed: ['bond_etf', 'crypto', 'stock']`; `{where}: unknown provider {value!r}; allowed: ['eodhd', 'binance', 'yahoo-csv']`; `{where}: kind {value!r} is not supported - only ['eod']; a non-EOD load is a new data contract, not a config value`.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-018 · refusal · basis both
If an `eodhd` source's symbol contains no `.`, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{where}: eodhd symbols must be canonical TICKER.EXCHANGE (e.g. AAPL.US, BTC-USD.CC), got {symbol!r} - bare tickers would blur store coordinates and the crypto/raw basis split`.

*Why:* bare tickers would blur store coordinates and the crypto/raw basis split

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-019 · refusal · basis logic
If window keys are misplaced or inverted, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `{where}: start/end apply to collector sources only; a CSV import is whole-file`; `{where}: path applies to yahoo-csv sources only`; `{where}: start {start} is after end {end}` (compared as normalised ISO strings).

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-020 · refusal · basis logic
If the modeled-source rules of the universe are violated, then the loader shall raise UniverseError with exactly one of: `asset '{name}': a modeled source must be enabled`; `asset '{name}': exactly one enabled source may be modeled = true, got {k}`; `asset '{name}': {k} enabled sources but none marked modeled = true - the binning's feeder must be deterministic (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md SS7.7)`; `asset '{name}': enabled but has no enabled source - nothing would feed the binning; to pause the asset, set enabled = false on the asset itself`.

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-021 · refusal · basis logic
If two assets share a name, then the loader shall raise UniverseError `{origin}: duplicate asset name(s) {sorted names}`; if two assets declare the same (exchange tag, symbol) store coordinate, then it shall raise `{origin}: store series {exchange}/{symbol} is claimed by both {first owner!r} and {second owner!r} - two assets may never write the same partition` (one asset may repeat a coordinate across its own sources).

*Why:* two assets may never write the same partition

*Realised by:* data_model  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation

### JDL-022 · refusal · basis logic
If an explicit universe path does not exist, then the command shall terminate with an unhandled FileNotFoundError traceback on stderr and exit code 1 (the error is not wrapped in the `{command}: ` prefix).

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: A universe path that does not exist is an unwrapped error

### JDL-028 · refusal · basis logic
If a collector request cannot succeed, then it shall raise CollectorError with exactly one of: `{label}: HTTP {status} after {attempts} attempts` (retryable status exhausted; attempts = the attempt count of JDL-027); `{label}: network failure after {attempts} attempts: {redacted error}`; `{label}: HTTP {status}: {first 200 characters of the body, token redacted as ***}` (any other non-200); `{label}: response is not JSON: {first 200 characters, redacted}`; the label is `eod {SYM}`, `splits {SYM}`, `div {SYM}` or `klines {symbol}`.

*Realised by:* data_model, sync_leg  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: A 404 on the bars fails the leg after the corporate actions were refreshed; collectors.feature: A 503 is retried five times, then the leg fails before any bar is fetched; collectors.feature: A bar endpoint answering something other than a JSON list fails the leg; collectors.feature: When both the actions and the bars would fail, the actions failure is what the leg reports

### JDL-030 · refusal · basis both
If the EODHD collector is constructed with no API key argument and an empty or unset EODHD_API_KEY, then construction shall raise ValueError `EODHD API key required: pass api_key= or set EODHD_API_KEY` before any session is opened.

*Why:* config errors must fail first, and without opening a session

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Unwrapped collector errors of the hand-run EODHD commands; collectors.feature: Without an EODHD key every EODHD leg fails and the CSV leg still lands

### JDL-051 · refusal · basis both
If the adjustment is asked to process a frame whose `price_basis` column holds any value other than `raw`, then it shall raise AdjustmentRefused `price_basis {sorted non-raw values} is already adjusted at the provider - applying split events would double-adjust (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §2)`.

*Why:* applying split events to pre-adjusted prices would double-adjust

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment, data_model, series_state  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: The adjust command refuses what it must not adjust

### JDL-052 · refusal · basis logic
If a split event's ratio is non-finite or <= 0, then the adjustment shall raise AdjustmentRefused `split {date} has degenerate ratio {ratio!r}`; if any `*_raw` column or `datetime` is missing it shall raise AdjustmentRefused `cannot adjust without immutable raw columns: missing {list}`.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment, data_model  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: A degenerate stored split ratio fails the leg before anything is written

### JDL-061 · refusal · basis logic
If any bar date cannot be parsed in the format of the first bar, then storing shall raise StoreError `unparseable dates cannot be stored: {list of at most the first 5 offending values}` and write nothing.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* store.feature: An import refuses what it cannot store

### JDL-085 · refusal · basis both
If an asset filter names an asset absent from the universe (disabled assets count as present), then selection shall raise SyncError `unknown asset {name!r}; universe has {sorted names}`; if a provider filter is not one of eodhd, binance, yahoo-csv, it shall raise `unknown provider {name!r}; allowed: ['eodhd', 'binance', 'yahoo-csv']`; if no leg survives, it shall raise `selection matched no enabled asset/source legs`; asset filters are checked (in the given order) before provider filters.

*Why:* a filter that matches nothing is a typo, not an empty day's work

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: Where an error is raised decides how the user sees it; sync.feature: Selection refusals of sync and status

### JDL-087 · refusal · basis both
If the sync tail is smaller than 1, then the sync shall raise SyncError `tail must be >= 1 session, got {tail}` before any selection or store access; the default tail is 10 sessions.

*Realised by:* data_model, sync_run  
*Verified by:* sync.feature: Selection refusals of sync and status; sync.feature: The tail window starts at the oldest of the newest N stored sessions

### JDL-142 · refusal · basis both
If `load` gets no `--asset-type` for a normalised symbol not ending in `.CC`, then it shall refuse with `load: {SYM}: asset_type is required (one of ['crypto', 'etf', 'stock']). The ticker carries no instrument-type signal - SPY, TLT, GLD and IBIT are ETFs spelled exactly like equities - so the old 'stock' default was a guess written into the store as a fact, and TLT is in this repo's universe as an explicit override because that guess got it wrong. Only EODHD's .CC crypto namespace is evidence enough to infer from`; if a `.CC` symbol is declared other than crypto, it shall refuse with `load: {SYM} is in EODHD's .CC crypto namespace but was declared asset_type={T!r}; that combination cannot be true, and guessing either way decides whether split adjustment runs on pre-adjusted prices (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md §2)`; a `.CC` symbol with no declaration is crypto; both refusals exit 1 before any fetch or store write.

*Why:* the suffix is evidence for crypto in one direction only: crypto does not imply .CC, and a ticker never says stock vs ETF

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment, data_model  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: The hand-run load normalises the symbol and refuses a declaration it cannot trust; decisions.feature: Where an error is raised decides how the user sees it

### JDL-159 · refusal · basis logic
If `export` is asked for a series the store does not hold (no year file under its exchange tag and symbol), then the command shall apply the export projection to the zero-row read-back frame without any guard and terminate with an unhandled traceback whose last stderr line is pandas' own `AttributeError: Can only use .dt accessor with datetimelike values. Did you mean: 'at'?` (the zero-row frame's `datetime` column is not datetimelike), with exit code 1, nothing on stdout and the output file not written - it is not a StoreError refusal.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: Exporting a series the store does not hold ends in pandas' own AttributeError; decisions.feature: The store commands on an absent series

### JDL-163 · refusal · basis logic
If `differential` is asked for a stored side the store does not hold (the A series, or the B series named by `--b-symbol`), then the command shall apply the seam projection to the zero-row read-back frame without any guard and terminate like JDL-159: an unhandled traceback whose last stderr line is `AttributeError: Can only use .dt accessor with datetimelike values. Did you mean: 'at'?`, exit code 1, nothing on stdout, no report file written - it is not a StoreError refusal (revision 2026-10-23 (wave 2): measured on the original, both sides).

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: The store commands on an absent series

## Command line: surface, output, exit codes (20)

### JDL-075 · cli · basis logic
When `export` writes its CSV, it shall write the frame with a header line and no index column, floats in shortest round-trip form (e.g. `19.84952380952381`, `100000.0`), int64 volumes as integers.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* seam.feature: Exporting a series whose volumes are all integral writes an int64 Volume; seam.feature: Exporting the two-split equity writes the adjusted mains with a float Volume

### JDL-083 · cli · basis logic
The differential report shall be the lines `differential: {A} vs {B} (relative tolerance {tol:g})`, `rows: {nA} in {A}, {nB} in {B}, {nC} dates in common`, for each side with unmatched dates `only in {label}: {n} date(s): {first 5 sorted, comma-separated}` plus ` (+{n-5} more)` when n > 5, then per column either `{col}: within tolerance (max {max rel:.3%})` or `{col}: {k}/{nC} beyond tolerance, worst {rel:.3%} on {date} ({A}={a!r}, {B}={b!r})` (numpy scalar repr, e.g. `np.float64(10.5)`, worst = first maximum), then `VERDICT: within tolerance, aligned` or `VERDICT: {cells} cell(s) beyond tolerance, {unmatched} unmatched date(s) - review before scale-out`.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* differential.feature: A stored series against a CSV with one changed cell and unmatched dates

### JDL-089 · cli · basis both
When no store path is given, the sync and status commands shall use the universe's `defaults.store` (relative to the working directory).

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: The status JSON envelope on stdout, with the universe's default store; sync.feature: The CLI dry run uses the universe's default store and still writes the summary

### JDL-131 · cli · basis both
The status command shall exit 1 when alerts_total > 0 and 0 otherwise; warnings and notes never change the exit code.

*Why:* exit 1 stops the venue's day before it publishes

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: A measured spread is always noted, warns strictly above the threshold, alerts when promoted; decisions.feature: Any alert sets exit 1 and flags the row ALERT; decisions.feature: Warnings alone flag WARN at exit 0; nothing flags ok; status.feature: A class disagreement on a healthy series warns without failing the day; status.feature: Never-filled series and the declared-class verdicts against the packaged evidence; status.feature: The cross-venue close spread warns strictly above its threshold, or alerts when promoted; status.feature: The status table of a filled, a mis-declared and a never-filled source

### JDL-132 · cli · basis logic
Without `--json`, the status command shall print per source report `{flag} {asset:>6} {exchange}/{symbol}: last {last_session or -}, {missed_sessions or -} missed, {rows or 0} row(s)` with flag `ALERT` (alerts), `WARN ` (warnings, no alert) or `ok   `, then `        res   {distinct} distinct / {sessions} traded, min tick {tick}, {flat_share:.2%} flat` when resolution exists, then `        ALERT {text}`, `        WARN  {text}`, `        note  {text}` lines; per pair `{flag} {asset:>6} cross-venue {a} vs {b}` and its ALERT/WARN/note lines; finally `{n} source(s)` + `, {p} venue pair(s)` (when any) + `, {k} alert(s)` + `, {w} warning(s)` (when any).

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* decisions.feature: Any alert sets exit 1 and flags the row ALERT; decisions.feature: Warnings alone flag WARN at exit 0; nothing flags ok; status.feature: The status table of a filled, a mis-declared and a never-filled source; status.feature: The status table of a pair and of a CSV-only selection

### JDL-133 · cli · basis both
The executable `jef-data` shall offer exactly the subcommands validate, sync-actions, load, adjust, import-csv, export, differential, sync, status and universe, with the flags and defaults of contracts/cli.md; a missing subcommand, unknown flag, missing required flag, invalid choice or non-numeric numeric flag shall be an argument error printed by the parser with exit code 2.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: Argument errors are the parser's, with exit code 2; cli.feature: Parser errors print the failing parser's usage and one error line; decisions.feature: Where an error is raised decides how the user sees it

### JDL-134 · cli · basis both
A refusal the command wraps (universe, selection, declaration and differential refusals) shall print `{command}: {message}` on stderr and exit 1 with nothing on stdout; any other error escaping a command shall print a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1.

*Why:* house pattern, not a traceback

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: The adjust command refuses what it must not adjust; cli.feature: Exporting a series the store does not hold ends in pandas' own AttributeError; collectors.feature: The hand-run load normalises the symbol and refuses a declaration it cannot trust; collectors.feature: Unwrapped collector errors of the hand-run EODHD commands; decisions.feature: The store commands on a filled raw-basis series; decisions.feature: The store commands on an absent series; decisions.feature: Where an error is raised decides how the user sees it; differential.feature: A differential with nothing to compare against is refused; seam.feature: Exporting a series with no stored rows fails without writing the file; sync.feature: Selection refusals of sync and status; universe.feature: A malformed universe is refused with its first violation; universe.feature: A universe path that does not exist is an unwrapped error

### JDL-135 · cli · basis logic
`validate CSV [--min-rows N]` shall read the CSV, print `{csv}: {rows} rows` then the validation report, and exit 0 when the report has no error, else 1.
