### JDL-136 · cli · basis logic
`universe [--universe PATH]` shall print, per asset, `{name} ({asset_class}, {currency}, threshold {threshold as float})` plus ` [disabled]` for a disabled asset, then per source `  {provider}: {path or symbol}` plus ` [disabled]` for a disabled source plus ` - {note}` when a note exists, and exit 0.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* universe.feature: The listing marks paused assets, switched-off sources and notes; universe.feature: The packaged universe lists its six pilot assets

### JDL-137 · cli · basis both
`import-csv --csv F --symbol S [--exchange yahoo] --asset-type {crypto,etf,stock} [--currency USD] [--store data]` shall import per JDL-070 into `exchange/symbol` and print `{csv}: {rows} row(s) -> {store}/market_data/exchange={exchange}/symbol={symbol}/ (price_basis=split_adjusted)` and exit 0; `--asset-type` is required.

*Why:* a Yahoo CSV carries no instrument type, so there is no evidence of any kind to infer from

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: An import into a chosen exchange tag keeps the declared labels; decisions.feature: import-csv overwrites, whatever the store held; store.feature: A Yahoo CSV import replaces the whole series and reports the CSV row count; store.feature: An import refuses what it cannot store

### JDL-138 · cli · basis logic
`export --symbol S [--exchange eodhd] --output F [--store data]` shall write the exported frame to F, print `{exchange}/{symbol}: {n} row(s) -> {output}` then the validation report of the exported frame, and exit 0 when that report has no error, else 1; exporting a series with no stored row shall fail with a traceback, exit 1 and no file written.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: Exporting a series the store does not hold ends in pandas' own AttributeError; decisions.feature: The store commands on a filled raw-basis series; seam.feature: Exporting a series whose volumes are all integral writes an int64 Volume; seam.feature: Exporting a series with no stored rows fails without writing the file; seam.feature: Exporting the two-split equity writes the adjusted mains with a float Volume; seam.feature: The export passes zero-volume rows through and the report announces the seam's drop

### JDL-139 · cli · basis both
`adjust --symbol S [--exchange eodhd] [--store data]` shall re-adjust the stored series with the stored splits of S and print `{exchange}/{symbol}: {rows} row(s) re-derived from *_raw with {k} split(s)` and exit 0; a split_adjusted series (AdjustmentRefused) or an empty series (StoreError) shall fail with a traceback and exit 1.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* adjustment.feature: The adjust command re-derives the mains from raw with whatever splits are stored; adjustment.feature: The adjust command refuses what it must not adjust

### JDL-140 · cli · basis both
`differential --a-symbol S [--a-exchange eodhd] [--b-symbol S2] [--b-exchange yahoo] [--b-csv F] [--tolerance X] [--output F] [--store data]` (tolerance default of JDL-082) shall compare the exported frame of a/S with the CSV F (preferred when both are given) or with the exported frame of b-exchange/S2, print the report (also written with a trailing newline to --output when given), exit 0 when ok and 1 on findings or unmatched dates, and refuse with `differential: pass --b-csv or --b-symbol` (exit 1) when neither is given.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* differential.feature: A differential with nothing to compare against is refused; differential.feature: A stored series against a CSV with one changed cell and unmatched dates; differential.feature: Two stored series that agree are aligned within tolerance

### JDL-141 · cli · basis both
`load --symbol S [--store data] [--from D] [--to D] [--asset-type T] [--currency USD] [--base-url URL]` shall construct the EODHD collector first (a missing key fails with a traceback, exit 1), normalise S, resolve the declaration per JDL-142, fetch from `--from` or else the day after the latest stored session (whole history when empty) up to `--to`, store the bars in APPEND mode into exchange tag `eodhd` (stored rows win over incoming rows on equal timestamps, only the incoming bars' years are rewritten; raw basis: with the stored splits and EODHD volume raw-ization), re-adjust a raw series that received bars or already had rows, and print `{S as given}: {n incoming bars} bar(s) ingested -> {store}/market_data/`.

*Realised by:* basis_and_adjustment  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: The hand-run load normalises the symbol and refuses a declaration it cannot trust; collectors.feature: Unwrapped collector errors of the hand-run EODHD commands

### JDL-143 · cli · basis logic
`sync-actions --symbol S [--store data] [--base-url URL]` (base URL default of JDL-029) shall sync the corporate actions of S per JDL-042 (EODHD key required; a missing key fails with a traceback, exit 1), print `{S}: {s} split(s), {d} dividend(s) -> {store}/corporate_actions/` and exit 0.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Unwrapped collector errors of the hand-run EODHD commands

### JDL-144 · cli · basis both
`sync [--universe P] [--store P] [--asset A]... [--provider P]... [--dry-run] [--tail N] [--force-actions] [--base-url URL] [--summary-json PATH]` (tail default of JDL-087) shall run the sync with its log lines on stdout, write the summary document (1-space indentation, keys sorted, trailing newline) to PATH after every run that returns - green, red and dry-run alike - and exit 0 when the run is ok, 1 when any leg failed, 1 with `sync: {message}` on stderr (and no summary) on a universe or selection refusal.

*Why:* a red run writes the summary too - the always-published breadcrumb

*Realised by:* sync_run  
*Verified by:* collectors.feature: Without an EODHD key every EODHD leg fails and the CSV leg still lands; sync.feature: A committed CSV leg whose file is missing fails that leg alone; sync.feature: Selection refusals of sync and status; sync.feature: The CLI dry run uses the universe's default store and still writes the summary

### JDL-145 · cli · basis both
`status [--universe P] [--store P] [--asset A]... [--provider P]... [--staleness N] [--jump-threshold X] [--window N] [--resolution-window N] [--resolution-k X] [--flat-k X] [--gap-k N] [--spread-threshold X] [--spread-alerts] [--json]` (integers N, floats X; defaults are those of JDL-116, JDL-124, JDL-122, JDL-123, JDL-121, JDL-129) shall print the JSON envelope or the table and exit per JDL-131; a universe or selection refusal shall print `status: {message}` on stderr and exit 1.

*Realised by:* status_run  
*Verified by:* status.feature: The status JSON envelope on stdout, with the universe's default store; status.feature: The status table of a filled, a mis-declared and a never-filled source; status.feature: The status table of a pair and of a CSV-only selection; sync.feature: Selection refusals of sync and status

### JDL-160 · cli · basis logic
The command line shall be declared as: a top-level parser with prog `jef-data`, the CLI module docstring as description (quoted in contracts/cli.md), the default help formatter, no epilog and the default `-h, --help`; one subparsers group with dest `command`, required, without metavar, title or help, so usage and help list the subcommand choices in braces; the ten subcommands added in the order validate, sync-actions, load, adjust, import-csv, export, differential, sync, status, universe, each created with its help string and no description; and every option with the option strings, dest, metavar, action, type, default, choices and help string of the contracts/cli.md "Parser surface" tables (the metavar is the upper-cased dest except `--summary-json`, whose metavar is `PATH`; choice options print `{crypto,etf,stock}`).

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: Every --help prints its verbatim text and exits 0; cli.feature: Parser errors print the failing parser's usage and one error line

### JDL-161 · cli · basis logic
When the command line cannot be parsed, the program shall print on stderr `usage: ` plus the formatted usage of the parser that failed (wrapped at the terminal width), then the line `{prog}: error: {message}` with prog `jef-data` or `jef-data <subcommand>`, print nothing on stdout and exit 2; arguments no parser recognises are reported by the top-level parser (top-level usage and `jef-data: error: unrecognized arguments: {arguments}`) even after a valid subcommand, and a missing subcommand reads `jef-data: error: the following arguments are required: command`.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: Parser errors print the failing parser's usage and one error line

### JDL-162 · cli · basis logic
When `--help` or `-h` is given to the top-level parser or to any of the ten subcommands, the program shall print on stdout exactly the corresponding block of contracts/cli_help.md (captured with an 80-column terminal: `COLUMNS=80`, or no terminal and `COLUMNS` unset), print nothing on stderr and exit 0.

*Realised by:* component  
*Verified by:* cli.feature: Every --help prints its verbatim text and exits 0

## The daily chain script (13)

### JDL-146 · chain · basis both
The chain `daily.sh` shall run under `set -euo pipefail` and read JEF_S3_BUCKET (required), JEF_ASSETS (default `AAPL BTC TLT NVDA TSLA IBM`, split on whitespace), JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST, ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4, JEF_TASK_VCPU, JEF_TASK_MEMORY_GB, JEF_RUN_STAMP and JEF_APP_DIR (default `/app`); EODHD_API_KEY passes through to the commands it runs; RUN_DATE = `date -u +%F`, STORE = `data`, OUT = `out/{RUN_DATE}`, DIAG = `{OUT}/.diagnostics`.

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last; chain.feature: A red sync stops the chain with its exit code after emitting, and the dashboard still publishes

### JDL-147 · chain · basis both
When JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST is empty or unset, the chain shall fetch `curl -s "${ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4:-}/task"` once (failure tolerated) and set JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST to Containers[0].ImageDigest, else Containers[0].ImageID, else `unknown` (also when parsing fails), and set JEF_TASK_VCPU to Limits.CPU and JEF_TASK_MEMORY_GB to Limits.Memory / 1024 (Python float text) only when unset and parsing succeeds, exporting both; JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST is exported in every case, before the exec guard.

*Why:* one metadata fetch for both facts; set-if-unset so the re-exec never recomputes and an external value passes through

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: Without a digest the chain reads it, and the task size, from the task metadata once

### JDL-148 · chain · basis both
The chain shall set JEF_RUN_STAMP to `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ` only when it is unset or empty and export it before the exec guard, so every stage of one invocation (and the re-exec) shares one stamp.

*Why:* the chain's start instant, captured once

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last; chain.feature: Arguments other than --inner are executed in place of the daily chain

### JDL-149 · chain · basis both
When the chain is invoked with arguments whose first is not `--inner`, it shall `exec` those arguments as a command (inheriting the digest and stamp exports) and run none of its own stages, traps or uploads; the command's exit code becomes the chain's.

*Why:* ECS cannot replace an ENTRYPOINT at run-task, so an override command arrives as arguments and must exec through instead of being swallowed

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: Arguments other than --inner are executed in place of the daily chain

### JDL-150 · chain · basis both
When invoked without arguments, the chain shall re-exec itself as `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=60 3600 "$0" --inner`; all stages run only in the `--inner` invocation.

*Why:* a wedged run must die loudly, not hold the lock all day

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last; chain.feature: Without a bucket the inner run stops before any stage

### JDL-151 · chain · basis logic
If JEF_S3_BUCKET is empty or unset in the inner run, then the chain shall stop with the shell parameter error whose text ends `JEF_S3_BUCKET must name the venue bucket` and exit code 1, before sourcing the externals, installing traps or running any stage.

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: Without a bucket the inner run stops before any stage

### JDL-152 · chain · basis both
The chain shall source `events.sh` and `dashboard.sh` from its own directory (`dirname "$0"`) before changing directory, then `cd` to JEF_APP_DIR, print `== jef daily {RUN_DATE} assets: {assets space-separated}` and create `{DIAG}` (`mkdir -p`); it uses only the externals' functions `jef_emit STAGE RC T0 T1 [args...]`, `jef_put STAGE`, `jef_attach_if_present PATH`, `jef_manifest_keys MANIFEST OUT` and `jef_publish_dashboard`, which read RUN_DATE, STORE, JEF_RUN_STAMP, JEF_S3_BUCKET, JEF_EVENT_DIR and JEF_DASH_DIR; the externals are given, not specified here.

*Why:* $0 is relative to the invoking directory, so dirname $0 stops resolving once the script changes directory

*Realised by:* component, daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last

### JDL-153 · chain · basis both
After sourcing, the chain shall install a TERM trap running `jef_emit "${STAGE:-unknown}" 143 "${STAGE_T0:-0}" "$(date +%s)"`, `jef_put "${STAGE:-unknown}"`, `exit 143`, and an EXIT trap running `jef_publish_dashboard` (which returns 0, so the run's exit code is preserved) - the dashboard therefore publishes on green and red exits of the inner run alike, never for an exec'd override.

*Why:* emit what the dying stage knows inside the 60 s grace; the dashboard publishes on every exit so the page shows a red day within minutes

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A TERM during a stage emits that stage with rc 143, exits 143 and still publishes the dashboard; chain.feature: A red sync stops the chain with its exit code after emitting, and the dashboard still publishes

### JDL-154 · chain · basis both
The chain shall first restore the store with `aws s3 sync s3://{bucket}/store/ data/ --only-show-errors` (a failure stops the chain with its exit code) and build the filter arguments `--asset A` for each asset in order.

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A failed store restore stops the chain with the restore's exit code; chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last

### JDL-155 · chain · basis both
The sync stage shall set STAGE=sync and STAGE_T0=`date +%s`, run `jef-data sync {filters} --store data --summary-json out/{RUN_DATE}/.diagnostics/sync.json` capturing its exit code, call `jef_emit sync {rc} {t0} {date +%s}` with `--attach {that file}` appended only when the file is non-empty, call `jef_put sync`, and exit with rc when rc is non-zero.

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last; chain.feature: A red sync stops the chain with its exit code after emitting, and the dashboard still publishes

### JDL-156 · chain · basis both
The status stage shall set STAGE=status, run `jef-data status {filters} --store data --json` once with its stdout both printed and written to `out/{RUN_DATE}/.diagnostics/status.json` (the pipeline's exit code is the status command's), emit and put the `status` stage like the sync stage, and exit with rc when non-zero.

*Why:* one evaluation, captured: running status twice would evaluate the freshness predicate at two instants

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last; chain.feature: Status alerts stop the chain before binning and publish nothing

### JDL-157 · chain · basis both
The binning stage shall set STAGE=binning and, per asset in order, run `jef-binning --asset A --store data --counter-start latest --counter-end latest --output-dir out/{RUN_DATE}/A`, find the first `run_manifest*.json` directly inside that directory, when found call `jef_manifest_keys {manifest} out/{RUN_DATE}/.diagnostics/binning-A.json`, call `jef_emit binning {a_rc} {a_t0} {t1} --asset A` plus `--manifest {m} --manifest-root out/{RUN_DATE} --manifest-prefix runs/{RUN_DATE}` when a manifest was found plus `--attach` of the keys file when non-empty, and stop the loop at the first non-zero rc; then call `jef_put binning` once and exit with that rc when non-zero.

*Why:* one ledger object for the stage, one emit per asset; a failing asset still emits

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last; chain.feature: The binning loop stops at the first failing asset, which is still emitted

### JDL-158 · chain · basis both
Only when every stage exited 0, the chain shall run `aws s3 sync data/ s3://{bucket}/store/ --only-show-errors`, `aws s3 sync out/{RUN_DATE}/ s3://{bucket}/runs/{RUN_DATE}/ --only-show-errors`, pipe `{JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST}` plus newline into `aws s3 cp - s3://{bucket}/runs/{RUN_DATE}/image_digest.txt --only-show-errors`, print `== green ({JEF_IMAGE_DIGEST})` and exit 0; a red stage publishes neither the store nor the run outputs.

*Why:* publish ONLY on green: a red run publishes nothing and the task exit code feeds the alarm

*Realised by:* daily_chain  
*Verified by:* chain.feature: A green run executes every stage in order and publishes last; chain.feature: A red sync stops the chain with its exit code after emitting, and the dashboard still publishes; chain.feature: Status alerts stop the chain before binning and publish nothing
